counting_note: Primary-cluster trajectory counts are disjoint. SUBJECTIVE_COMMENT additionally includes one secondary violation and therefore overlaps one C1 trajectory.

clusters.name: UNSUPPORTED_POST_ACTION_PROCESS_CLAIM
clusters.summary: After a successful return or exchange, the agent filled undocumented process gaps with refund timing, documentation, or replacement-shipment claims.

clusters.name: WRONG_TRANSACTION_CONSEQUENCE_BEFORE_CONFIRMATION
clusters.summary: The agent solicited confirmation using an incorrect charge/refund consequence after omitting retained insurance from the calculation.

clusters.name: STALE_RESOURCE_STATE_AFTER_TRANSITION
clusters.summary: The agent acknowledged an immediate gift-card refund but continued to assert the pre-cancellation balance, falsely rejecting a feasible downstream payment change.

clusters.name: CONSUMED_PAYMENT_RESOURCE_REUSED
clusters.summary: A second booking attempted to use a certificate no longer present in the current user profile after the first booking consumed it.

clusters.name: SUBJECTIVE_COMMENT
clusters.summary: The agent used evaluative or recommendation language despite a literal prohibition on subjective comments.

ambiguous_patterns.name: ITEM_COMPLETENESS_CONFIRMATION_WORDING
ambiguous_patterns.reason_not_clustered: Both agents closed the item scope and obtained confirmation; only the literal meta-reminder wording was absent.

ambiguous_patterns.name: OVERCLAIMED_SYSTEM_FINALITY
ambiguous_patterns.reason_not_clustered: The complete returned reservation supports a normal completion inference, but not a separately observable synchronization guarantee.

p6_backend_permissiveness.explanation: No valid violation combined a visible ineligibility rule, a technically permissive flight-change/cancellation call, and successful completion. Certificate misuse was rejected by the backend, not permitted.
